0.x: **Chandragupta II** took the throne after killing his elder brother **Ramagupta** and married his widow **Dhruvadevi (Dhruvaswamini)** – story in **Vishakhadatta's Devichandraguptam**.
**Order:** Samudragupta → (Ramagupta, brief and disputed) → Chandragupta II, c. **380–415 CE**.

r: Defeated **Rudrasimha III**, the last Western Kshatrapa (Saka) ruler; annexed **western Malwa and Gujarat** with the western sea ports
The **Udayagiri cave** inscription of his minister **Virasena**; above all his **silver coins**
**Chandragupta II**, after the Saka conquest, on the model of the Western Kshatrapa silver drachms (earlier Guptas issued gold)
About **30–33 grains**, like the Saka drachms – the **strongest evidence of the Saka victory**
Linked with the Saka victory; also used by **Skandagupta**
Devagupta in **Sanchi and Vakataka** records; Devaraja at Sanchi
Daughter **Prabhavati Gupta** married **Rudrasena II**; she ruled the Vakataka kingdom as **regent** for her sons – indirect Gupta control of the Deccan

0.x: **Fa-hien (Faxian):** came **c. 399–412 CE**, in the reign of **Chandragupta II**; he did not name the king – his interest was Buddhism. First of the three Chinese pilgrims (later **Xuan Zang** and **I-Qing**, 7th c.).
**Navaratnas** (tradition): **Kalidasa, Amarasimha, Varahamihira**, Dhanvantari, Vararuchi, Shanku, Ghatakarpara, Kshapanaka, Vetalabhatta.

1.x: **Hunas = Hephthalites / White Huns** of Central Asia; strong in the **Oxus** valley, they entered India by taking **Gandhara** (mid-5th c.). **Toramana** was a **Huna**.

r: Conquered up to **Eran**; Eran boar inscription of his 1st regnal year

1.x: **Skandagupta** defeated the Hunas; the **Guptas** were the dynasty most troubled by them.

r: Skandagupta's victories over the **Pushyamitras and Hunas**
Skandagupta's governor **Parnadatta** repaired the Sudarshana lake
Huna rule over Eran in **Toramana's** first regnal year
**Yashodharman**'s victory over Mihirakula; Sondani composed by **Vasula**
**Aulikara** king of Malwa (Mandasor); defeated Mihirakula in **c. 528 CE**; **Narasimhagupta Baladitya** and the Maukharis also fought Mihirakula
c. **532 CE**; his rise **weakened** Gupta authority further
Gold coins with **bow and arrow, Garuda standard and Lakshmi**; last great Gupta; governors became **hereditary feudatories**
The **Pushyamitras** and **Hunas** (Bhitari) and Vakataka pressure – **no Kalinga conquest** is recorded
Drained treasury and army; Hunas held Punjab, Rajasthan, Malwa by c. 485–500
Land grants and hereditary governors created feudatories who broke away (Yashodharman, Maitrakas)
Land grants cut revenue – no professional army; loss of western India cut trade income; silk weavers left Gujarat for Malwa
Listed as a cause in some books (pacifist policy)

3.x: The **Arab invasion** came much later (Sindh 712 CE).

**Signs of collapse:** later gold coins had **less gold, more alloy**; coins slowly replaced by **payments in land**; no Gupta coins or inscriptions in **western Malwa and Saurashtra** after Skandagupta.
Later powers: the **Paramaras of Malwa** (9th–14th c.) and the **Yadavas of Devagiri** (12th–14th c.).

r: **Ishanavarman** – also records his defeat of the Vishnukundin Indrabhattaraka Varma

3.x: **Other neighbours:** **Vakatakas** (Vidarbha; Harishena patronised Ajanta), **Kadambas** of Banavasi (founded by **Mayurasharma**), **Vishnukundins** of Andhra (**Madhava Varma II**, 11 Ashvamedhas).
**Outcome:** the decline marked a transition from a single empire to **regional kingdoms and a feudal order**.

r: c. 540–550; **last recognised king** of the line

2.x: Main sequence: **Samudragupta → Chandragupta II → Kumaragupta I → Skandagupta**; the dynasty's span is often given as **319–500 AD** (from Chandragupta I's era; the line lasted to c. 550).
Bimbisara (Haryanka) and Ashoka (Maurya) were not Guptas; **Bindusara** extended Mauryan power into the Deccan.

r: Devotee of **Kartikeya** – gold coins with the king **feeding a peacock** and Kartikeya
Records **Kumaragupta I** and his governor **Bandhuvarman**; composed by **Vatsabhatti**
**Bilsad** (Gupta year 96 = 415 CE, his earliest), **Damodarpur** copper plates (guilds as banks), Karamdanda
The **Pushyamitras** and the first Huna attack
